parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of LoanController does presentation work: it defines the request shapes, calls the services, renders with renderLoan and maps results to HTTP status codes. However, it also coordinates a business workflow. After every lend or return it records a history event by calling LoanHistoryService.note after the LendingService call. That makes the controller the only place enforcing the business rule that every lend or return is logged, so other ways of creating or returning a loan would skip it. It also decides the return timestamp with new Date(), which affects the fine calculation. This sequencing belongs in the business layer (a domain service or use case), not in presentation. Confidence is moderate because controllers that call several services are sometimes considered acceptable.

violations.message: lend() and giveBack() coordinate a business workflow: LendingService call followed by LoanHistoryService.note('lent'/'returned'). The rule that every lend or return must be recorded in history is a business rule and belongs in the business layer, not the presentation controller.
giveBack() picks the return date with `new Date()`, which affects the fine calculation. This decision belongs in the business layer.
